To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PA activity was higher, in tumors from postmenopausal women, in those that were ER + PR +, than in those exhibiting the other subsets of joint ER and PR expression, and that the presence of ER was the only factor which emerged as significantly associated with PA in the analyses of pre‐menopausa women, whereas PR and age (inversely) were the only factors to do so in the analyses of postmenopausal patients.
the expression of functional ER and PR in breast tumor samples are statistically associated with PA activity.
the expression of functional ER is associated with PA activity in breast cancer samples, and that this is particularly so in the case of tumors from post‐Menopausal women.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the expression and regulation of plasmin‐related proteases in human cancer cells.
the relationship between plasminogen activation and estrogen receptor expression in human breast cancer, and with the possible role of the latter as a determinant of plasmin activity.
the possible role of PA in breast cancer, and its relationship to steroid hormone receptors and other clinical and histopathologic variables.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PA activity in human primary breast cancer is associated with the presence of PR, and to a lesser extent with ER, and that the association is stronger in post‐menopaulous than in pre‐menopuasual patients.
ER and PR are not independent variables with respect to PA activity, and that PA activity is not an independent predictor of the clinical behavior of breast cancer.
PA activity in primary breast tumors is a function of the expression of PR and of ER, and that the latter effect is only evident in post‐menopauxal patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PA activity may be an independent marker for the presence of ER and/or PR in female breast cancer, and therefore may have some predictive value in the assessment of prognosis and treatment.
PA activity is a marker of estrogen‐dependent growth of breast tumor cells.
PA activity is a marker of estrogen receptor status in breast tumors from post‐ menopausal women, and may be a useful adjunct for predicting the response of these tumors to endocrine therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PA activity is not a reliable marker of tumor aggressiveness in breast cancer.
the presence of ER and PR in breast tumors, and the absence of PR in ER‐positive tumors, are associated with increased levels of plasmin‐activatable PA.
PA activity is an independent prognostic factor in ER +PR+ patients, particularly those from the post‐menopausa group.
